cells.tense: You are holding, in the present, what the last change made and left worth keeping.
cells.act: accept what is offered for what you gave
cells.ask: Let whatever someone next hands you — a thanks, a hand, a portion set aside — come all the way in, and take it without adding anything back on top.
cells.core:
A change came through and something of it is here, holding: a routine that works, a room people land in, a tie that outlasted the rough stretch. You keep it steady, and steady is the rare part. Underneath, the draw toward what you actually want is quiet. You can see it in small leanings — a subject you keep reading about, a person you keep finding reasons to see.

When you hand something over, the same size usually comes back, and you take it. That much of you is working. Let it keep working by letting one thing be given to you outright — not matched, not returned, not squared. Receive it plainly and say so. The direction you steer by stays lit on exchanges like that, and it dims when you pay everything back.
cells.sheetLine: What the change left standing, you are still holding.
cells.verb: keeping what the change left standing

cells.tense: You are bracing for a version of this that hasn't been written yet.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Visit the thing that keeps pulling you. Stand in it up close, then leave it there. Not a plan, not a later version — just the visit.
cells.core:
The light you steer by has gotten busy. Every version of what you want is already furnished — the room, the work, the outcome, the way it will feel when it lands — and today gets spent inside those versions instead of at the workbench. You still keep what you won; lately you are keeping a lot of drawings.

What you want is not the drawing. It is the thing, and it shows itself only at arm's length. Go stand in the pull once — the class you keep almost signing up for, the place you keep almost going — without deciding anything afterward. The version in your head will thin out on contact, and what remains will be smaller and truer. That is the one worth keeping.
cells.sheetLine: The light is still there. You're packing for it early.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Hold one direction you already chose against a single push off it — you know which push is coming — and keep the heading.
cells.core:
Something got cleared out, and instead of standing on what was left, you are still facing the doorway it went through. From there nothing pulls, because every route looks like it leads back to the same room. You show up to the day and the day is fine. No direction is at work in you while you do.

Direction does not come back from thinking about direction. It comes back from keeping hold of something you already chose when somebody leans on it — the plan you won't move off your evening, the limit you set, the thing you said you'd keep doing and quietly let go slack. Hold one of those against one push. The rest of the pull returns after you have a heading, not before it. Don't hunt for the feeling. Stand on the decision.

cells.tense: You are reading from a chart you drew and calling it the sky.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Settle a call you have been sitting on the same day you notice it, and act — no case built for anyone, no announcement.
cells.core:
You keep other people steady, and none of it carries your name. You call what they get from you just how things are, and you call the direction you hold onto keeping busy. Underneath both, something is doing clear work — sorting what matters, protecting what was won, saying no to the pull that would carry off the whole structure. That work is yours. You have been describing it as something that happens to you.

Deciding is how you take the pen back. Settle an overdue call, done the same day, without building a case for it in front of anyone. The same holding you give everybody else is the same holding you can stand on. Do it once and the chart stops being sky. Nothing needs announcing.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering this. You've been filing it as sky.
